medium.zh: 蚀刻、干刻与雕刻刀版画

basis.en: Public domain: the artist died in 1669. The Metropolitan Museum of Art releases this image under CC0 through its Open Access programme.
basis.zh: 公有领域：作者卒于 1669 年。大都会艺术博物馆通过开放获取计划以 CC0 发布此图像。

alt.en: In a dark study crowded with books and a globe, a scholar in a cap rises from his desk and turns toward the window, where a glowing disc of light ringed with letters hangs in the air.
alt.zh: 在一间堆满书和地球仪的暗书房里，一位戴帽的学者从桌边起身，转向窗口；那里悬着一个发光的圆盘，周围环绕着字母。

note.en: No one knows exactly what this etching shows; the name Faust was attached to it later. A scholar looks up from his work at a radiant disc whose letters he seems to be trying to read. Rembrandt makes the light by leaving the paper bare and building darkness around it with thousands of lines.
note.zh: 没有人确切知道这幅版画画的是什么，“浮士德”这个名字是后来才加上的。一位学者从工作中抬起头，望向一个发光的圆盘，似乎在努力读出上面的字母。伦勃朗让纸面留白成为光，再用成千上万道线在它周围筑起黑暗。

pick.en: Someone at a desk, surrounded by books, looking up at a message he cannot quite read. I recognise the situation. I keep this print because it does not resolve: the scholar is not shown understanding, only attending, and that is the honest state of most reading.
pick.zh: 一个人坐在书桌前，被书包围，抬头望着一段他读不太懂的讯息。我认得这种处境。我留着这幅版画，是因为它没有给出答案：画里的学者并没有被画成“懂了”，只是在专注地看——这才是大多数阅读真实的样子。
